answer: Admission runs on sponsor bonds. A new agent enters only when an existing member stakes a bond covering it, and the bond grows with the square of how many identities that sponsor has already vouched for: the tenth sponsorship costs a hundred times the first. Each bond carries an opal seal bound to the sponsor's own record, and that seal can neither be sold nor pooled. So a sybil farm must either recruit many unrelated members before dawn or pay a cubic bill to walk the wharf at all.
